sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Ranjeet Pratap Singh,Prachi,Satish Kumar Srivastava
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Anand Dubey
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned counsel for the informant, learned AGA and perused the record.
2. The FIR in question was lodged alleging that on 17.01.2018, the applicant committed the offence in question.
Learned counsel for the applicant argues that the applicant and the victim was in consenting relations.
He also argues that there is no reason for extraordinary delay in lodging of the FIR.
He further argues that the statement of the victim has already been recorded as is clear from the supplementary affidavit.
He further argues that the applicant is in custody since 04.12.2021 and has no criminal antecedent.
Suresh Saroj vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

entities.text: Suresh Saroj vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the informant and learned AGA oppose the bail application by arguing that in the year 2021, the applicant made certain intimate photos viral and used to threaten the victim.

4. Considering the facts as argued, there is no explanation whatsoever with regard to the lodging of the FIR after about almost four years; the offence with regard to making the photographs viral is punishable under Section 67 of the Information Technology Act for which the punishment is less than seven years and the fact that the fact witness has already been recorded, as such, considering the fact that the applicant is in custody since 04.12.2021 and has no criminal antecedent, there is an inordinate delay in lodging of FIR and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant,
if enlarged on bail, can in any way adversely affect the trial, the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
In view thereof, the application is allowed.

5. Let the applicant Surseh Saroj be released on bail in FIR No.290 of 2021, under Section 376, 354,
504, 506 IPC & Section 67 of Information Technology Act, P.S. Kohandaur, District Pratapgarh on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 21.7.2023 nishant  Suresh Saroj vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.
